cells.tense: The heart is open right now, and nothing has been poured into it yet.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: When a pull shows up this week, stay with it an hour and then stop. Leave it unsorted — no yes, no no.
cells.core:
You can feel something before you know what it is, and that is where you are. A conversation, a project, a plan — one of them is tugging at you and you have not named it. The pull is the beginning, and you are letting it stay a pull, not rushing to close it into a decision.

That openness is also what you are made of. What you are becoming shows through most clearly when you let a thing interest you before you have decided what it is for. So follow a pull a little way, and hold there. The interest does not have to turn into a plan, and letting it stay open is not the same as avoiding the choice.
cells.sheetLine: The pull is the beginning, and you are not rushing it.
cells.verb: opening to what hasn't arrived yet
cells.place: where what you are comes out as what you do

cells.tense: You will have the whole thing settled before it has a chance to arrive.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Choose something you have been leaving half-done and give it a real ending. Call it finished and act on that, once.
cells.core:
An opening is barely here and you are already bracing for what happens after it. The feeling has not shown up and you have decided how it should land, what it should become, who it is for. You are completing who you are supposed to be before the feeling has shown you anything. Readiness gets spent on the shape of things rather than on the things themselves.

What settles it is finishing something cleanly. Not a fresh direction — one thing already in motion, given a real end. When a thing is finished on purpose, the bracing loses its job, and there is room again for what has not yet arrived.
cells.sheetLine: You have decided the ending before the feeling lands.

cells.tense: The moment to open has already passed, and you are standing there still.
cells.act: bring the possibility all the way into form
cells.ask: Bring one of the ideas you keep turning over into something you can point to — make it once, at whatever size it comes out.
cells.core:
You are set up to feel what is coming — that part of you is intact. But something that mattered got put down before it could finish, and since then you have been watching from behind the door. The readiness is there, and it has nowhere to land. Pulling back has been a way of not adding anything more to the pile, and it has started to look like who you are.

There is a way back that does not ask you to feel more. Make what has only ever existed as a thought into something once, at whatever size it comes out. You do not have to arrive anywhere. A single finished small act is enough for the door to swing open from the other side.

cells.tense: You are already receiving and feeding what is around you, without having noticed the doing.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: This week, when someone hands you something, take it at the size it comes. Do not give back twice the size.
cells.core:
The way you take things in is easy to miss because it runs in the background. You open to what people bring before they have finished bringing it, answer what is needed before it is asked, and call that being receptive, or just being around. From the inside it does not look like a role. From the outside it is why certain rooms stay warm.

What is missing is the other half of the exchange. Take what someone offers at the size it was offered, and do not add to it. Receiving something whole, without matching it, is not a debt. It is the other side of the thing you already do well, and it has been waiting for you to see that it counts.
cells.sheetLine: You already receive what is around you — let an exchange land once.
